  the output of ip6tables-save as another file.
  note: No list of listening sockets was read, so every open port is judged as if a service uses it.
  Add the output of "ss -tulnp" as another file to tell used ports from unused ones.

  Fix first
    1. F1   INPUT accepts new connections to any port                                   +15, grade B
    2. F2   Unreachable rules in filter/INPUT                                                     +5
    3. F3   22/tcp is open to any source                                                          +5

  Findings

  HIGH     F1   INPUT accepts new connections to any port                                        -15
                Rule #2 in filter/INPUT (-j ACCEPT) accepts them from any source, whatever the
                policy of the chain is. Every port that no rule names is open: a service that
                listens on one, now or later, is reachable at once.
                filter/INPUT #2:  -j ACCEPT
                fix  This rule accepts every packet that reaches it, so the rules after it and the
                     policy of the chain decide nothing. Add rules for the traffic that is needed,
                     with a tested way back, then delete it.
                     Delete the rule that accepts everything:
                       iptables -D INPUT 2

  HIGH     F2   Unreachable rules in filter/INPUT                                                 -5
                Rules #3-#5 (3 rules) are never reached: rule #2 (-j ACCEPT) ends the chain for all
                traffic before. 2 of them are DROP or REJECT and have no effect.
                filter/INPUT #2:  -j ACCEPT
                fix  Delete the rules that are never reached, or move those that must apply above
                     the rule that ends the chain.

  HIGH     F3   22/tcp is open to any source                                                      -5
                IPv4: accepted by filter/INPUT rule #1.
                filter/INPUT #1:  -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
                fix  If the clients are known, accept only their addresses. If SSH must stay open to
                     any source, limit new connections for each source: the limit counts every
                     source by itself, so one client cannot lock out the others, and it does not
                     touch established sessions.
                     Replace the rule with one for the known clients:
                       iptables -R INPUT 1 -s <trusted-cidr> -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
                     Or drop the connections of a source that opens more than 10 a minute, in front
                     of the rule:
                       iptables -I INPUT 1 -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4 -j DROP

  MEDIUM   F4   FORWARD accepts traffic that no rule names                                        -5
                No rule refuses it, and the policy of filter/FORWARD is ACCEPT. This matters when IP
                forwarding is enabled (net.ipv4.ip_forward, net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding): the host
                then routes packets between its networks without a filter.
                fix  Set the policy to DROP after the forwarding paths that are needed have rules.
                     Deny forwarding by default (IPv4):
                       iptables -P FORWARD DROP

  INFO     F5   OUTPUT default policy is ACCEPT
                All outbound traffic is allowed. This is the usual setup; an OUTPUT allowlist can
                limit what a compromised service is able to reach.

  Open to any source
    tcp  22 · all ports that no rule names
    udp  all ports that no rule names

    Landlock is not available

       5 -s 10.0.0.0/8 -p tcp --dport 5432 -j ACCEPT
